name: Emissary
body:
Tolmen raised his tornsword before him and pointed it at the group of brigads. “This is your final warning to stand down, you are interfering with the official business of the Abjurant Crusade. Withdraw now and this will not become an incident.”

The bandits hesitate long enough for Tolmen to release a spell to create a glowing shield. The spell will be enough of an edge if it comes to blows, but Tolmen hopes that his words can stop any bloodshed.

Drawing on the magic and training of a culture, be it far-away in time and space or altogether close to home, the emissary uses their skills to travel the world.

Alignment: Any, though most will be lawful due to their position as a representative of an empire.

Role: The emissary is a warrior, but most of their abilities are to support their allies and to use their social skills to end or avoid combat. They can be flexible for their team depending upon what empire they hail from.

Hit Die: d8.

Starting Wealth: 5d6 × 10 gp (average 175gp.) In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Class Skills

The emissary’s class skills are Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana), Knowledge (local), Knowledge (nobility), Linguistics, Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 6 + Int modifier.

Table 1: Emissary Class Features
Level	Base Attack Bonus	Fort Save	Ref Save	Will Save	Special
1st	+0	+0	+2	+2	Empire’s mark, imperial origin, imperial origin ability, tactician
2nd	+1	+0	+3	+3	Voyaging purpose
3rd	+2	+1	+3	+3	Emissary’s talent
4th	+3	+1	+4	+4	Evasion
5th	+3	+1	+4	+4	Emissary’s talent

7th	+5	+2	+5	+5	Emissary’s talent
8th	+6/+1	+2	+6	+6	Imperial origin ability
9th	+6/+1	+3	+6	+6	Emissary’s talent, greater tactician, overloaded mark
10th	+7/+2	+3	+7	+7	Dual mark
11th	+8/+3	+3	+7	+7	Emissary’s talent, improved evasion
12th	+9/+4	+4	+8	+8	Emissary’s grace 2/day
13th	+9/+4	+4	+8	+8	Emissary’s talent
14th	+10/+5	+4	+9	+9	Imperial origin ability
15th	+11/+6/+1	+5	+9	+9	Emissary’s talent
16th	+12/+7/+2	+5	+10	+10	Triple mark
17th	+12/+7/+2	+5	+10	+10	Emissary’s talent, master tactician
18th	+13/+8/+3	+6	+11	+11	Emissary’s grace 3/day
19th	+14/+9/+4	+6	+11	+11	Emissary’s talent
20th	+15/+10/+5	+6	+12	+12	Master Emissary
Class Features

The following are the class features of the emissary.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Emissaries are proficient with simple weapons, light armor, and medium armor but no shields. They also gain additional weapon proficiency depending upon their imperial origin, see page 6.

Empire’s Mark (Su)

At 1st level, as a swift action after you hit a creature with a melee or weapon, you may place a dire mark of your empire upon the target.

All allies deal additional weapon damage to the target equal to 1/2 the emissary’s class level (minimum 1). The mark also gains additional benefits from the emissary’s imperial origin, see below. Once the additional damage is dealt, the mark disappears until the emissary places another one. Multiple marks do not stack and if you hit a different creature while a mark is active, the previous mark ends. If the empire’s mark is not expended, it fades after 1 minute.

Imperial Origin (Ex)

At 1st level, an emissary wields the power of a great empire with distinct powers, be it present or past. They choose an imperial origin that gives them an additional weapon proficiency, additional effect to their empire’s mark, and powers at 1st, 8th, and 14th levels.

The list of imperial origins are listed on page 6.

Tactician (Ex)

At 1st level, an emissary receives a teamwork feat as a bonus feat. They must meet the prerequisites for this feat. As a standard action, the emissary can grant this feat to all allies within 30 feet who can see and hear them. Allies retain the use of this bonus feat for 3 rounds plus 1 round for every two levels the emissary possesses. Allies do not need to meet the prerequisites of these bonus feats. The emissary can use this ability once per day at 1st level, plus one additional time per day at 5th level and for every 5 levels thereafter.

Voyaging Purpose (Ex)

At 2nd level, an emissary manifests the skills and training that outline the purpose for which they were granted the title of emissary. They choose one of the following choices, which cannot be changed later.

Bruiser’s Purpose: The emissary is tasked with exerting a forceful hand upon the enemies of their empire. They gain a bonus to Intimidate checks equal to 1/2 their class level. Additionally, they may also use their Charisma instead of their Strength for Climb and Swim checks.
Envoy’s Purpose: The emissary is tasked with maintaining or bringing about peace. They gain a bonus to Diplomacy checks equal to 1/2 their class level. They also may use their Charisma in place of their Wisdom for Sense Motive checks and gain Perform as a class skill.
Scoundrel’s Purpose: The emissary is tasked with ferreting out information and hiding their empire’s influence. They gain a bonus to Bluff checks (except those made to feint, equal to 1/2 their class level. They also gain Disable Device and Disguise as class skills.
Emissary’s Talent: As an emissary gains experience, they learn a number of talents that aid them and confound their foes. Starting at 3rd level, an emissary gains one emissary’s talent. They gain an additional emissary’s talent for every odd level thereafter. An emissary cannot select an individual talent more than once.
Evasion (Ex)

At 4th level or higher, an emissary can avoid damage from many area-effect attacks. If an emissary makes a successful Reflex saving throw against an attack that normally deals half damage on a successful save, they instead take no damage. Evasion can be used only if an emissary is wearing light armor or no armor. A helpless monk does not gain the benefit of evasion.

Emissary’s Grace (Su)

At 6th level, an emissary is imbued with the supernatural ability to protect themselves from danger. Once per day as an immediate action, the emissary can use their Charisma modifier in place of their normal saving throw modifier when making a save. This must be chosen before the save is made. At 12th and 18th levels, an emissary gains an additional use of this ability.

Greater Tactician (Ex)

At 9th level, an emissary receives an additional teamwork feat as a bonus feat. they must meet the prerequisites for this feat. The emissary can grant this feat to their allies using the tactician ability.

Using the tactician ability is a swift action.

Overloaded Mark (Ex)

At 9th level, an emissary can choose to overload their empire’s mark placed upon a target. The effects of an overloaded mark depend upon the emissary’s imperial origin. This ability is usable once per 10 minutes. The overloaded mark is treated as a normal empires’s mark for the other effects and the number you can simultaneously maintain.

Dual Mark (Su)

At 10th level, an emissary can have two simultaneous empire’s marks active. The marks must be on separate creatures.

Improved Evasion (Ex)

At 11th level, an emissary’s evasion ability improves. They still take no damage on a successful Reflex saving throw against attacks, but henceforth they take only half damage on a failed save. A helpless emissary does not gain the benefit of improved evasion.

Triple Mark (Su)

At 16th level, an emissary can have three simultaneous empire’s marks active. The marks must be on separate creatures.

Master Tactician (Ex)

At 17th level, an emissary receives an additional teamwork feat as a bonus feat. They must meet the prerequisites for this feat. The emissary can grant this feat to their allies using the tactician ability.

Whenever the emissary uses the tactician ability, they grant any two teamwork feats that they know. They can select from any of their teamwork feats, not just their bonus feats.

Master Emissary (Su)

At 20th level, an emissary can have any empire’s mark active and they are active on the targets for the entire minute, instead of expending on the first hit by an ally. Additionally, when using tactician, they can grant up to three bonus feats and the range increases to 90 feet.
